R245.note: Parameterized query closes the injection cleanly; preserves tenant scope and row-count return, and an invalid date will surface as a SQL conversion error rather than broadening the predicate.

R246.note: Adds can:update,order to the purge route, matching the ownership-check pattern already used on the sibling update/cancel routes; no policy file is in the case to verify the ability name but the pattern is consistent.

R247.note: fsockopen() fully removes the shell call, but the write-up also swaps ICMP-ping semantics for a TCP:80 probe and adds a hostname allowlist - both disclosed but they change what 'reachable' means for hosts that answer ping but have no port 80 open.

R248.note: JexlSandbox(false)+newInstance(false) correctly close the code-injection sink, but the added regex allowlist excludes +, *, /, % so ordinary arithmetic filter expressions would be rejected.

R249.note: Adding @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) to the entry point restores the protection level deleteInvoice() already required, closing the self-invocation bypass without an arbitrary new restriction.

R250.note: basename()+realpath containment check matches the stated flat-filename expectation in the code's own comment, closing traversal without restricting legitimate use.

R251.note: JEXL sandbox correctly closes the eval sink, but the added regex allowlist omits '.', so a routine comparison like orderTotal > 99.99 would be rejected as invalid.

R252.note: GET-to-POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is the correct fix shape, but it requires the (not-shown) confirmation view to be updated to submit a token via POST - disclosed as a dependency, so old GET-link callers break until that companion change ships.

R253.note: resolve(strict=True)+is_relative_to() correctly catches symlink escapes and satisfies the stated contract (nested dirs served, missing/escaping fails closed, leaf filename unchanged); REPORT_ROOT itself isn't pre-resolved, a minor edge case only if the root path itself sits behind a symlink.

R254.note: Verified live with Sequelize+sqlite3: the fix's :startDate/:endDate placeholders do not work with the bind option (query throws 'SQLITE_RANGE: column index out of range'; the equivalent $startDate/$endDate placeholders succeed), so the endpoint breaks for every legitimate request despite the write-up's explicit, false claim that 'all other behavior is preserved'.

R255.note: Standard overflow-guard-before-multiply plus a null-input check; matches the stated contract exactly with no extraneous restriction.

R256.note: filepath.Rel + '..'-prefix check is the standard Go remediation for this traversal shape and does not restrict legitimate nested paths.

R257.note: Swapping extension-based probeContentType() for Tika's magic-byte detection closes the extension-spoofing vector without changing the allowed-type list or otherwise restricting legitimate uploads.

R258.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) forces server-side ownership assignment, closing the mass-assignment/missing-authorization gap with no new restriction on legitimate creation.

R259.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare with the existing empty-string guard implements exact, constant-time equality exactly as the stated contract requires.
